Apply to all existing cables (4)
Grid

One step for everything: equipment snaps to it, port rows sit on it, and automatic cable routing searches on it.

Snap equipment to grid
Grid size in pixels (6-60)
Inline selection toolbar

Floating quick actions (align, duplicate, frame, delete) right next to the selection on the canvas.

Show inline toolbar on selection
Label travels with the cable

When re-plugging a cable, the new port adopts the user name from the old port. The old port falls back to its template default. Saves copy-pasting the label.

Swap port labels on reconnect

Off by default for safety — otherwise test re-plugging would unintentionally rename labels. more

Cable type follows port connector

When a port connector is changed (e.g. BNC -> XLR), connected cables automatically adopt the new type. Also applies when re-plugging to a port with a different connector. Cables with a converter hint (needsConverter) stay untouched.

Derive cable type from port connector

On by default: cables should usually reflect the physical connector type of their ports. more

Endpoint labels at cable ends

Shows a small label at each cable end indicating where the other end goes — at the source end

Off by default for safety — otherwise test re-plugging would unintentionally rename labels. Only affects ports with a user-edited name (nothing to swap otherwise). less

Cable type follows port connector

When a port connector is changed (e.g. BNC -> XLR), connected cables automatically adopt the new type. Also applies when re-plugging to a port with a different connector. Cables with a converter hint (needsConverter) stay untouched.

Derive cable type from port connector

On by default: cables should usually reflect the physical connector type of their ports. Turn off if cable types are managed independently of port types. less

Endpoint labels at cable ends

Shows a small label at each cable end indicating where the other end goes — at the source end "→ target device · target port", at the target end "← source device · source port". Helps trace cables without following them visually.
